Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

bitest

Test a binary success probability exactly

Stata 

bitest b = 0.5

R stats 

stats::binom.test(sum(data$b),nrow(data),p=0.5)

Differs from Stata Returns an exact two-sided binomial test. The code assumes the displayed binary sample has no missing values; Stata additionally prints lower- and upper-tail probabilities.

Stata reference · R reference

bitesti

Run an exact binomial test from counts

Stata 

bitesti 20 7 0.5

R stats 

stats::binom.test(7,20,p=0.5)

Differs from Stata Uses an exact two-sided binomial test from the supplied count and total. R reports one htest result; Stata additionally displays both one-sided probabilities.

Stata reference · R reference

ci

Compute a Student-t confidence interval for a mean

Stata 

ci means y

R stats 

stats::t.test(data$y)$conf.int

Differs from Stata Returns only the selected confidence limits, not Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns. Match nonmissing sample size, confidence level and the explicit interval method.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a Clopper-Pearson proportion interval

Stata 

ci proportions b, exact

R stats 

stats::binom.test(sum(data$b),nrow(data))$conf.int

Differs from Stata Returns only the selected confidence limits, not Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns. Match nonmissing sample size, confidence level and the explicit interval method.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a Wilson score interval for a proportion

Stata 

ci proportions b, wilson

R stats 

stats::prop.test(sum(data$b),nrow(data),correct=FALSE)$conf.int

Differs from Stata Returns only the selected confidence limits, not Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns. Match nonmissing sample size, confidence level and the explicit interval method.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a normal-theory variance interval

Stata 

ci variances y

R stats 

(length(data$y)-1)*stats::var(data$y)/stats::qchisq(c(0.975,0.025),df=length(data$y)-1)

Differs from Stata Returns only the selected confidence limits, not Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns. Match nonmissing sample size, confidence level and the explicit interval method.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a normal-theory standard-deviation interval

Stata 

ci variances y, sd

R stats 

sqrt((length(data$y)-1)*stats::var(data$y)/stats::qchisq(c(0.975,0.025),df=length(data$y)-1))

Differs from Stata Returns only the selected confidence limits, not Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns. Match nonmissing sample size, confidence level and the explicit interval method.

Stata reference · R reference

cii

Compute a mean interval from summary statistics

Stata 

cii means 50 10 2

R stats 

10+c(-1,1)*stats::qt(0.975,49)*2/sqrt(50)

Differs from Stata Computes confidence limits from the displayed summary inputs. The R result omits Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns; the stated method and confidence level determine the interval.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute an exact proportion interval from counts

Stata 

cii proportions 20 7, exact

R stats 

stats::binom.test(7,20)$conf.int

Differs from Stata Computes confidence limits from the displayed summary inputs. The R result omits Stata sample-size and point-estimate columns; the stated method and confidence level determine the interval.

Stata reference · R reference

ksmirnov

Compare two empirical distribution functions

Stata 

ksmirnov y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::ks.test(data$y[data$g=="a"],data$y[data$g=="b"],exact=FALSE)

Differs from Stata The two-sample form uses a grouping variable; a one-sample test instead requires a fully specified reference CDF.

Stata reference · R reference

ktau

Test Kendall rank association

Stata 

ktau y x

R stats 

stats::cor.test(data$y,data$x,method="kendall",exact=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Uses the asymptotic Kendall test. Tie adjustments and the reported tau variant must match; R returns one htest object rather than Stata full concordance summaries.

Stata reference · R reference

kwallis

Test equality of distributions across groups

Stata 

kwallis y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::kruskal.test(y~g,data=data)

Differs from Stata Computes the tie-corrected Kruskal-Wallis chi-square approximation. R returns an htest object without Stata group rank-sum summaries.

Stata reference · R reference

median

Run a two-group median test

Stata 

median y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::chisq.test(table(data$g,data$y>stats::median(data$y)),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Tests independence of group and the above-pooled-median indicator. The example assigns observations tied at the median to the lower category; align Stata ties() handling before comparison.

Stata reference · R reference

nptrend

Test an ordered trend in proportions

Stata 

nptrend b, group(g) carmitage

R stats 

{ sample <- stats::na.omit(data[c("b", "g")]); successes <- tapply(sample$b, sample$g, sum); totals <- as.vector(table(sample$g)); stats::prop.trend.test(successes, totals, score = as.numeric(names(successes))) }

Differs from Stata Aggregates binary b by ordered numeric g; group values are the Cochran-Armitage scores in both programs.

Stata reference · R reference

oneway

Compare group means with Bonferroni adjustment

Stata 

oneway y g, bonferroni

R stats 

stats::pairwise.t.test(data$y,data$g,p.adjust.method="bonferroni",pool.sd=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Uses the ordinary equal-variance one-way model or pooled pairwise t tests as shown. R object layout differs and does not reproduce every Stata tabulate column or comparison display.

Stata reference · R reference

Fit one-way analysis of variance

Stata 

oneway y g, tabulate

R stats 

stats::aov(y~factor(g),data=data)

Differs from Stata Uses the ordinary equal-variance one-way model or pooled pairwise t tests as shown. R object layout differs and does not reproduce every Stata tabulate column or comparison display.

Stata reference · R reference

prtest

Run an uncorrected large-sample one-proportion test

Stata 

prtest b == 0.5

R stats 

stats::prop.test(sum(data$b),nrow(data),p=0.5,correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Disables the R continuity correction for the normal-approximation proportion test. R reports a chi-square statistic whose square root is the absolute Stata z; signed direction requires the group order.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare two proportions without continuity correction

Stata 

prtest b, by(g)

R stats 

stats::prop.test(tapply(data$b,data$g,sum),as.vector(table(data$g)),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Disables the R continuity correction for the normal-approximation proportion test. R reports a chi-square statistic whose square root is the absolute Stata z; signed direction requires the group order.

Stata reference · R reference

prtesti

Compare proportions from aggregate sample sizes

Stata 

prtesti 100 0.4 120 0.5

R stats 

stats::prop.test(c(40,60),c(100,120),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Disables continuity correction. R returns a chi-square test; Stata reports a signed z and one-sided probabilities, although the two-sided p-values correspond for the same counts.

Stata reference · R reference

ranksum

Compare independent distributions with the rank-sum test

Stata 

ranksum y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::wilcox.test(y~g,data=data,exact=FALSE,correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Aligns the requested exact or uncorrected asymptotic Wilcoxon calculation. Tie handling, group ordering and reported rank-sum versus U-statistic conventions must be aligned.

Stata reference · R reference

Use exact rank-sum inference without ties

Stata 

ranksum y, by(g) exact

R stats 

stats::wilcox.test(y~g,data=data,exact=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Aligns the requested exact or uncorrected asymptotic Wilcoxon calculation. Tie handling, group ordering and reported rank-sum versus U-statistic conventions must be aligned.

Stata reference · R reference

sdtest

Test one normal population standard deviation

Stata 

sdtest y == 3

R stats 

{ y <- data$y[!is.na(data$y)]; degrees <- length(y) - 1; statistic <- degrees * stats::var(y) / 3^2; c(chisq = statistic, df = degrees, p.value = 2 * min(stats::pchisq(statistic, degrees), stats::pchisq(statistic, degrees, lower.tail = FALSE))) }

Differs from Stata Normal-theory variance test against population SD 3, with nonmissing sample degrees of freedom.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare two unpaired sample variances

Stata 

sdtest y == x

R stats 

stats::var.test(data$y,data$x)

Differs from Stata Uses a normal-theory variance-ratio or chi-square test. R returns test components in an htest object or vector; Stata also reports one-sided alternatives and additional confidence limits.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare variances of two independent normal samples

Stata 

sdtest y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::var.test(y~g,data=data)

Differs from Stata Uses a normal-theory variance-ratio or chi-square test. R returns test components in an htest object or vector; Stata also reports one-sided alternatives and additional confidence limits.

Stata reference · R reference

sdtesti

Compare variances from sample sizes and standard deviations

Stata 

sdtesti 30 . 2 40 . 3

R stats 

{ f <- 2^2/3^2; c(F=f,p.value=2*min(stats::pf(f,29,39),stats::pf(f,29,39,lower.tail=FALSE))) }

Differs from Stata Summary-input normal-theory variance ratio with SDs 2 and 3 and N=30 and N=40; dots omit unused means.

Stata reference · R reference

signrank

Use a paired signed-rank test with ties

Stata 

signrank y = x

R stats 

stats::wilcox.test(data$y,data$x,paired=TRUE,exact=FALSE,correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Asymptotic paired signed-rank test without continuity correction. Zero-difference handling and tie corrections depend on the R version; align these conventions with Stata before comparing p-values.

Stata reference · R reference

signtest

Test the median paired difference using signs

Stata 

signtest y = x

R stats 

{ difference <- data$y - data$x; difference <- difference[!is.na(difference) & difference != 0]; stats::binom.test(sum(difference > 0), length(difference), p = 0.5) }

Differs from Stata Drops missing pairs and zero differences, then performs the exact binomial sign test; its CI concerns the positive-difference probability.

Stata reference · R reference

spearman

Base R alternative for Spearman rank association

Stata 

spearman y x

R tidystata 

tidystata::spearman(data, y, x)

Differs from Stata Uses the Stata 18+ four-moment beta p-value with normal fallback; constant variables remain undefined in tidystata. Align the nonmissing sample.

Stata reference · R reference

swilk

Test univariate normality with Shapiro-Wilk

Stata 

swilk y

R stats 

stats::shapiro.test(data$y)

Differs from Stata Computes the Shapiro-Wilk W test; R permits 3 to 5000 nonmissing observations. Stata also displays transformed statistics and uses its own approximation and sample-size rules.

Stata reference · R reference

symmetry

Test symmetry in a matched binary table

Stata 

symmetry rater1 rater2

R stats 

stats::mcnemar.test(table(data$rater1,data$rater2),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata For a 2 by 2 table this is the uncorrected McNemar test; larger-table symmetry needs a different procedure.

Stata reference · R reference

tabi

Run a Pearson test from immediate cell counts

Stata 

tabi 12 8 \ 5 15, chi2

R stats 

stats::chisq.test(matrix(c(12,8,5,15),nrow=2,byrow=TRUE),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Builds the stated table by rows and disables continuity correction for Pearson chi-square. R returns an htest object rather than Stata contingency-table output.

Stata reference · R reference

tabulate

Test association in a two-way count table

Stata 

tabulate g b, chi2

R tidystata 

tidystata::tab2(data, g, b, .chi2 = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Prints Pearson's chi-squared test and Cramer's V below the table.

Stata reference · R reference

2 more examples and alternatives

Test association in a two-way count table

Stata 

tabulate g b, chi2

R stats 

stats::chisq.test(table(data$g,data$b),correct=FALSE)

Differs from Stata table excludes missing observations and unused factor levels can affect dimensions. The R htest object provides the selected Pearson or Fisher test without Stata row and column percentage displays.

Stata reference · R reference

Run a Fisher exact test for a two-way table

Stata 

tabulate g b, exact

R stats 

stats::fisher.test(table(data$g,data$b))

Differs from Stata table excludes missing observations and unused factor levels can affect dimensions. The R htest object provides the selected Pearson or Fisher test without Stata row and column percentage displays.

Stata reference · R reference

ttest

Test a mean against a specified value

Stata 

ttest y == 8

R stats 

stats::t.test(data$y,mu=8)

Differs from Stata Selects pooled, Welch or paired inference explicitly. R returns an htest object and may reverse the reported difference when factor-level order differs; match group order and the nonmissing sample.

Stata reference · R reference

Test paired mean differences

Stata 

ttest y == x

R stats 

stats::t.test(data$y,data$x,paired=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Selects pooled, Welch or paired inference explicitly. R returns an htest object and may reverse the reported difference when factor-level order differs; match group order and the nonmissing sample.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare two independent means with pooled variance

Stata 

ttest y, by(g)

R stats 

stats::t.test(y~g,data=data,var.equal=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Selects pooled, Welch or paired inference explicitly. R returns an htest object and may reverse the reported difference when factor-level order differs; match group order and the nonmissing sample.

Stata reference · R reference

Compare two means using Welch unequal-variance inference

Stata 

ttest y, by(g) unequal

R stats 

stats::t.test(y~g,data=data,var.equal=FALSE)

Differs from Stata Selects pooled, Welch or paired inference explicitly. R returns an htest object and may reverse the reported difference when factor-level order differs; match group order and the nonmissing sample.

Stata reference · R reference

Compute a 90 percent interval for a mean

Stata 

ttest y == 8, level(90)

R stats 

stats::t.test(data$y,mu=8,conf.level=0.90)

Differs from Stata Selects pooled, Welch or paired inference explicitly. R returns an htest object and may reverse the reported difference when factor-level order differs; match group order and the nonmissing sample.

ttesti

Run a one-mean t test from summary statistics

Stata 

ttesti 30 10 2 8

R stats 

{ t <- (10-8)/(2/sqrt(30)); c(t=t,df=29,p.value=2*stats::pt(-abs(t),29)) }

Differs from Stata Computes the one-sample t statistic, degrees of freedom and two-sided p-value from the supplied summaries. The R vector omits the confidence interval and one-sided probabilities.
